stories.headline: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson (ankle) vs. Bengals; Tyler 'Snoop' Huntley to start
stories.summary: The Baltimore Ravens have ruled QB Lamar Jackson out of Sundays game vs. the Cincinnati Bengals as he continues to deal with a high ankle sprain. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley will get the start.
stories.body:
BALTIMORE -- The Baltimore Ravens ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals, which means the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player will miss his third straight game.

On Saturday, the Ravens downgraded Jackson, who had been listed as questionable with a high left ankle injury after being limited all week in practice.

Tyler "Snoop" Huntley, who is 6-8 as a fill-in starter for the Ravens, will replace Jackson in an early critical AFC North game for Baltimore. After a disappointing loss at the Cleveland Browns last Sunday, the Ravens are looking to avoid falling to 0-2 in the division for the first time in 19 years.

After Friday's practice, Jackson didn't look like a quarterback who was close to full strength, limping to the lectern for his media session. He was also not seen as players walked off the field Friday, which suggests he did not finish practice.

Jackson said Friday that he was "heading in the right direction" and the decision would come down to pain tolerance.

"If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play," Jackson said. "But if I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, I'm not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and get hit, that's not helping my team at all."

Jackson injured his ankle on the last offensive snap before halftime in a win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. It looked like Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson II's shoulder landed on the outside of Jackson's left ankle, which caused it to bend awkwardly.

In returning to practice this week, Jackson acknowledged it hurts when he tries to run and plant his foot.

"It's just like trying to run ... can't put too much pressure [on the left foot]," Jackson said.

This month, Huntley led the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 12 before struggling in a 13-10 loss at the Browns on Sunday.

The Ravens' offense has lacked consistency without Jackson. In 14 quarters with Jackson this season, the Ravens have scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns. In 10 quarters with Huntley, Baltimore has totaled 40 points and four touchdowns.

This marks the second straight season in which Jackson has missed multiple games due to injury. Last season, he missed three straight games due to a hurt hamstring.

On Friday, he expressed regret rushing back from it because he was never truly healthy the rest of last season.

"I feel like that was dumb a little bit because I was still hurting," Jackson said. "I'm trying to help my team win, but I'm not to my full capability or not even close to it."

The loss of Jackson is a significant one for Sunday's game between the Ravens (4-2) and Bengals (3-2). Since 2019, the Ravens are 0-3, including the playoffs, against the Bengals without Jackson as their starting quarterback.

stories.headline: Dele Alli proves Spurs' good luck charm at Stamford Bridge again
stories.summary: Dele Alli was the hero during Tottenham's win at Chelsea in 2018 and he provided good luck for his old club on Saturday after he watched on at Stamford Bridge.
stories.body:
Dele Alli was the hero during Tottenham's win at Chelsea in 2018 and he provided good luck for his old club on Saturday after he watched on at Stamford Bridge.

An own-goal by Mike Penders and Mathys Tel's superb solo effort inspired Spurs to only a second victory at Chelsea in the Premier League era for a statement result for Roberto De Zerbi's new-look group.

One of those in attendance was former Tottenham attacker Dele, who posted on his Instagram story a selfie at Stamford Bridge alongside ex-Chelsea captain John Terry.

Dele, 30, has not played since a spell with Como during the 2024-25 season, but has been active on social media in recent weeks and teased his followers with an image asking "who can guess where I'm going?" before it was followed by an image of Stamford Bridge.

A shot alongside Terry was sent out pre-match and Dele then filmed the scoreboard as Spurs went ahead in the 77th minute.

- Tottenham's rare win at Chelsea signals progress under De Zerbi

- James Maddison's injury woes return, forced off for Tottenham vs. Chelsea

- Cole Palmer sent off for first time, Chelsea reach unwanted red card milestone

And the one-time England international poked fun at Chelsea at full-time with a picture on his story that was captioned "empty seat here now" with Terry nowhere to be seen as Dele savoured Tottenham ending their Stamford Bridge hoodoo.

stories.headline: UFC 333 live results, analysis for Volkanovski vs. Evloev, Yan vs. Dvalishvili
stories.summary: ESPN MMA contributors break down all the action from UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi.
stories.body:
Two UFC titles will be on the line at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, on Saturday, as featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski faces Movsar Evloev in the main event, and men's bantamweight champion Petr Yan takes on Merab Dvalishvili in the co-main event at UFC 333.

Volkanovski, who is in his second featherweight title reign, beat Diego Lopes by unanimous decision in his two most recent Octagon appearances. Evloev, undefeated in professional MMA, has won every UFC fight by decision.

The co-main event will be a rubber match between Yan and Dvalishvili. Dvalishvili won the first meeting in March 2023, then Yan won the next fight in December 2025 to claim the championship. When the pair enter the Octagon, it will be the 20th trilogy in UFC history.

stories.headline: Nashville SC wins 1st MLS Supporters' Shield title, eyes points record
stories.summary: Nashville SC clinched the 2026 MLS Supporters' Shield title after a 2-0 victory at CF Montréal on Saturday, winning the trophy for the first time in club history.
stories.body:
Nashville SC clinched the 2026 MLS Supporters' Shield title after a 2-0 victory at CF Montréal on Saturday, winning the trophy for the first time in club history.

The clinching goals came from the club's top scorer, Sam Surridge, and captain Hany Mukhtar.

Surridge struck the opening goal in the 51st minute, finishing at the second attempt after his initial header had been saved. Mukhtar then made sure of the decisive points in the 76th minute, capitalizing on a defensive giveaway and sliding in to finish low into the net.

- Miami coach praises Messi's 'commitment' to play after award in Spain

- Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or? We simulated the voting process to find out

Major League Soccer awards the Supporters' Shield to the club that accumulates the most points across the 34-game regular season. With 70 points in 31 games, Nashville has an unassailable lead in the overall standings with three regular-season games remaining.

The Vancouver Whitecaps and Inter Miami are Nashville's nearest challengers, 15 points back with four games to play.

"The locker room celebration is quite joyous at the moment," head coach BJ Callaghan said in his postgame news conference.

"It's a huge step forward for the club and for the city and the connection that we have with the supporters. That's the name of the trophy. It's a testament to the work that's been done, leading with the owner's vision, and kind of the day-to-day process that we continue to abide by."

Nashville could yet surpass Miami's MLS points record of 74, achieved in its 2024 Supporters' Shield-winning season.

As well as points, Nashville leads MLS in wins (21), fewest goals conceded (23) and goal differential (plus-43).

The team has scored 66 goals so far this season, the second-highest count in the Eastern Conference after Inter Miami. Surridge and Mukhtar played an integral role in the team's attack, with Surridge scoring 18 goals and Mukhtar adding 17.

Offseason arrival Cristian Espinoza also contributed heavily in the final third, providing 14 assists.

Nashville entered MLS as an expansion team in 2020, alongside Inter Miami, working diligently to become a competitor in the league. The team won its first trophy in 2025 when lifting the US Open Cup, before adding a second with this year's Supporters' Shield.

Callaghan, a former U.S. men's national team assistant and interim head coach, now becomes the first coach since Oscar Pareja in 2016 to win the US Open Cup and Supporters' Shield within a two-year span.

By winning the Supporters' Shield, Nashville secured home-field advantage throughout the MLS Cup playoffs and a spot in the 2027 edition of the Concacaf Champions Cup.

Nashville is the only MLS team unbeaten at home in 2026 and tied the league record for home wins (14) and home winning streak (10).

"Anytime we get an opportunity to play in front of our home fans, we are motivated," Callaghan said. "That is the connection that we have to the city, our club, and to the supporters. And we love playing at home. We know that people will come and support us, and sell GEODIS Park out. So it just makes it even more special."

He added: "We know that we've got more work to do."

Saturday's result also eliminated Montreal from playoffs contention.

stories.headline: How the Valkyries stole Game 4 on the road to even WNBA Finals at 2-2
stories.summary: Golden State won Game 4 in Atlanta, held Angel Reese to eight points and take home-court advantage back to Ballhalla.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- And we're all tied up.

The Golden State Valkyries made some changes in their starting lineup, built a 16-point lead and then held off the Atlanta Dream to win Game 4 67-62 and knot the WNBA Finals at 2-2.

The series shifts to San Francisco for Monday's Game 5 (8 p.m.) at Chase Center.

ESPN was on site Saturday and provided postgame analysis and updates and highlights from courtside.

Jump to:

Postgame analysis | Relive the action

(2) Golden State Valkyries 67,

(4) Atlanta Dream 62
How the Valkyries won the game: It really started with the lead they built before halftime, where they jumped ahead by as many as 16, the Dream's largest deficit of the postseason. Golden State rocked Atlanta back on its heels for the first time in a while, mixing in some zone defense, forcing turnovers and dominating the offensive glass.

In a role reversal from the past two games, the Dream committed 14 first-half turnovers, which Golden State turned into 16 points. Kaila Charles and Tiffany Hayes entered the starting lineup for Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini and did their part, Charles finishing with a plus/minus of plus-14 and Hayes adding 13 points. Zandalasini was still impactful coming off the bench, with a plus/minus of plus-20.

At halftime, the Valkyries had 40 field goal attempts to the Dream's 19 -- pretty much a guaranteed loss if you are Atlanta. Golden State finally managed to slow down Angel Reese, who finished 2-for-12 from the field for eight points, with nine rebounds, four fouls and six turnovers.

Atlanta technically won the second half by 11 but couldn't get over the hump. The Dream shot just 33% on the night and 4-for-23 from 3, and still took 18 fewer shots than the Valkyries. And they let a ton of points get away at the free throw line, where they went 22-for-31.

What the win means for Golden State: The Valkyries take this series back home having stolen one on the road and evening things up to avoid going down 3-1, which would have felt nearly insurmountable. And from here, as Kiah Stokes pointed out, it's basically a best-of-three series where they'll have home-court advantage for Game 5 and, if necessary, Game 7.

Which team has the edge going into Game 5: After the Valkyries didn't look like themselves the previous two games, especially defensively, this was a confidence-instilling performance that they are very much still in this series. Coach Natalie Nakase said going into Game 4 that she couldn't let her team down, and with the adjustments and game plan she came up with for Saturday, she did not. While the Valkyries lost Games 2 and 3 by a combined 40 points -- and even this win was a bit of a grind -- what matters is the series is tied at 2-2 and now they will play back in front of their incredible environment at Ballhalla. -- Alexa Philippou

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton edges Max Verstappen to go quickest in final practice at United States Grand Prix
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli faces a Ferrari-shaped threat to his hopes of clinching the Formula 1 world championship in Texas as Lewis Hamilton topped final practice at the United States Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli faces a Ferrari-shaped threat to his hopes of clinching the Formula 1 world championship in Texas as Lewis Hamilton topped final practice at the United States Grand Prix.

The Scuderia have brought an upgraded package to Austin and it helped Charles Leclerc claim a practice double on Friday.

Hamilton's prancing horse was on top in Saturday's practice session, 0.168 seconds ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen with Leclerc in third.

Antonelli claiming the crown in the Lone Star State would be a tall order; he would need to win Sunday's race and hope that George Russell finishes lower than ninth and Hamilton lower than fifth.

The first part of that equation looks set to be a challenge as his rivals showed their prowess in the final running ahead of qualifying.

Antonelli was fourth-fastest after his best lap was deleted for a breach of track limits, one place ahead of Mercedes teammate Russell.

Sunday represents the 20-year-old's first shot at clinching the crown but, with a 102-point lead and only 150 left up for grabs ahead of this weekend's tussle at the Circuit of the Americas, it appears merely a matter of when the Italian becomes champion.

- Ferrari's Charles Leclerc sets pace in second practice from Kimi Antonelli

- COTA boss addresses driver concerns ahead of United States GP

- Carlos Sainz on F1 season concluding in Middle East: 'Very difficult to be convinced right now'

"Obviously, I'm in an incredible position," Antonelli, who will become the sport's youngest champion, said ahead of the weekend.

"But, of course, I still have to keep going, and the mindset is always the same: whenever I go on track, I want to be at the top and try to win as much as possible.

"Whether I win the championship this weekend, next weekend [Mexico] or in Brazil. Let's see. But it's not over until it's over."

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was sixth-fastest, with Audi's Nico Hülkenberg behind. Piastri's teammate Lando Norris rounded out the top eight.

Qualifying for Sunday's race goes green at 10 p.m. BST / 5 p.m. ET.

stories.headline: Mavericks' Cooper Flagg out for home opener with mild left shoulder sprain
stories.summary: Mavericks star forward Cooper Flagg had an MRI that revealed a mild left shoulder sprain, the team announced. He will not play against the Spurs.
stories.body:
DALLAS -- Mavericks star forward Cooper Flagg had an MRI on Saturday morning that revealed a mild left shoulder sprain, the team announced.

Flagg has been ruled out of Saturday night's home opener against the San Antonio Spurs. He will be reevaluated next week.

The reigning Rookie of the Year, Flagg suffered the injury when he took a flagrant foul by Indiana Pacers forward Aaron Nesmith on a breakaway late in the second quarter of the Mavericks' road win Friday night. Flagg exited moments later and did not return to the game.

Flagg, 19, was off to a fast start in his second season. He scored 32 points in Wednesday's loss to the Houston Rockets, the highest-scoring performance ever by a teenager in a season opener. He had 14 points, six assists, five rebounds, three steals and a block in 17 minutes before exiting against the Pacers.

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: Future Chiefs star in PNG as Samoa slaughter Kumuls
stories.summary: Samoa have issued a World Cup statement by hammering Papua New Guinea 64-6 on home soil.
stories.body:
Jarome Luai and Brian To'o were showered with gifts in their first match in Papua New Guinea since signing with the PNG Chiefs, as Samoa dismantled the Kumuls in a 64-6 win.

At the National Football Stadium, which Luai and teammate Brian To'o will call home in 2028, Samoa survived an early scare to keep their unbeaten start to the tournament intact.

The local fans unfurled banners for the Chiefs-bound pair on Saturday, where Luai recorded four try assists and To'o crossed for a try.

At fulltime the pair were mobbed and handed bilum bags from local supporters as they gave away all their match jerseys and shorts to members of the crowd.

"Since the day that we touched down in PNG, the love, the respect, and hospitality that the country has shown us ... it's one of those feelings that you can't describe," Samoa captain Junior Paulo said.

"You've got to be here to witness it firsthand.

"There's a bigger picture for us and seeing the scenes post game and what it means to the people.

"The bus ride here, seeing the kids' smiles on their faces, you just can't get that anywhere else besides here."

After thrashing France in their tournament opener, Samoa have wracked up two big wins and will face Tonga in Sydney next Sunday.

Both sides will look to guarantee their passage to the semi-finals as Group B/C winners.

But Samoa will head there having received a thorough test at the hands of the Kumuls in dizzying heat and humidity in Port Moresby.

For the first 40 minutes, PNG held their gloves up and at one stage led when halfback Bailey Biondi-Odo cancelled out Sua Fa'alogo's opener and Rhyse Martin - playing his final Test on home soil - kicked the conversion.

The excitement was palpable and one of the loudest cheers from the 15,088-strong crowd came when PNG five-eighth Gairo Voro hammered Luai.

"We knew it was going to be a bit of a kamikaze battle coming up against the Kumuls," Paulo said.

Samoa opened up a 14-6 gap at halftime with further tries to Stephen Crichton and Spencer Leniu.

PNG lost Jack de Belin midway through the first half with a rib injury in another blow for coach Jason Demetriou, who was forced to rule out two of his only players with NRL experience in Nene Macdonald (illness) and Luca Moretti (rib).

"I think it took its toll, the first half we were very physical, and we went after the contest, losing Jack was big as well," said Demetriou, who could only name 18 fit players in his 19-man squad.

"When we're under pressure like that we don't have that experience to try to fight it back and win it back but some boys have to learn that - that's the brutal truth."

The Kumuls, who face England in Wollongong on Friday in their final group game, were unable to call-up Cooper Bai, Xavier Coates and Lachlan Lam due to injury, and without so many of their top-line names Samoa racked up 50 second-half points.

As Samoa's players were handed presents from the crowd at fulltime Martin - PNG's record pointscorer - was chaired off in his final home game for the Kumuls.

"It meant a lot to me, for my team to do that for me," the forward, who will move into an off-field role with the Chiefs, said.

"I thank them for that, and I thank our coach and the PNG fans for making it so special for so long."

stories.headline: Packers activate RB Josh Jacobs for 2026 debut
stories.summary: Packers running back Josh Jacobs will make his 2026 season debut against the Lions after spending the first six weeks on the NFL's commissioner exempt list.
stories.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs will make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the Detroit Lions after spending the first six weeks on the NFL's commissioner exempt list.

Green Bay added him to the active roster from exempt status Saturday. The NFL took Jacobs off the exempt list Monday.

The NFL's investigation of Jacobs for potential violations of the personal conduct policy following his arrest earlier this year on misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor destruction of property charges remains active, and a suspension could be equal to or greater than the number of games he already missed. The six games he has missed would be credited toward any suspension.

For now, Jacobs is cleared to play.

Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to the charges resulting from the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and reached a deferred judgment agreement on the property damage charge.

Without Jacobs, the Packers have had the worst running game in the NFL, ranking last in rushing yards per game at 59.8 yards. Jacobs was the Packers' leading rusher the previous two seasons, ranking eighth in the league in combined rushing yards (2,258) and tied for fourth in rushing touchdowns (28) during the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

The Packers also signed WR/KR Coleman Owen to the active roster off the practice squad, elevated edge rusher Arron Mosby from the practice squad for game day, and activated defensive tackle Jordon Riley off the physically unable to perform list.

stories.headline: Lone'er Kavanagh shoots into flyweight title talk with devastating finish at UFC 333
stories.summary: England's Lone'er Kavanagh catapulted himself into flyweight title contention on Saturday with a devastating Round 1 finish of Ramazonbek Temirov in Abu Dhabi.
stories.body:
England's Lone'er Kavanagh catapulted himself into flyweight title contention on Saturday with a devastating Round 1 finish of Ramazan Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi.

Coming into the fight as the No. 6 ranked flyweight in the world, Kavanagh, fighting out of London, put on a counter-attacking clinic securing the TKO win with a picture-perfect left uppercut with 30 seconds left on the clock in the first round.

The start of the contest saw Temirov come out of the gates fast, with his hard-hitting reputation preceding him. The Uzbek let a series of wild overhands, right hooks and haymakers fly early on, with some reaching their target.

But Kavanagh chose to fight behind his jab with his hands up and didn't let the few big shots that got through deter him.

That game plan provided the ultimate reward near the end of the first round as he dropped his shoulder in reaction to a Temirov left hook and let off a destructively quick left uppercut that rocked Temirov, and ultimately signalled the end of the fight.

From there, Kavanagh unleashed a flurry of punches at devastating speed to eventually put Temirov on the ground and with his back to the contest, before referee Mike Beltran stepped in to call it.

"Firstly, Abu Dhabi, thank you so much for having me, I love you guys, its an awesome country," Kavanagh said in the cage after the fight.

"I have an amazing team behind me. We work hard day in, day out to get these results. Trust in God's plan and we got it done."

Asked if it was his plan to capitalise on Temirov's fast, heavy output style, Kavanagh confirmed that it was his intention to stay on the outside as well as outlining that the flyweight belt is next on the agenda.

"Yeah exactly that, we've learned from previous mistakes, one of those is keeping my hands up, so I kept my hands up and made sure I can counter," he added.

"Obviously I'm here for that belt and respectfully anyone can get it, and yeah I'm here for that belt."

With the UFC announcing on Saturday that flyweight champion Joshua Van's next title defence will come against Manel Kape at UFC 336 in January, Kavanagh will fancy himself as being next in line.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 43
Goals: 40
Assists: 18

Oct. 17: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami
Messi scored twice in four minutes as Miami won 3-1 in Atlanta.

After Germán Berterame opened the scoring just before halftime, Messi doubled Miami's lead in the 56th minute, exchanging passes with Berterame before weaving past a defender and firing a low left-footed shot into the net.

Messi struck again in the 60th minute, latching on to a pass from Luis Suárez before beating his marker and slotting past goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos. The brace took Messi's MLS-leading tally to 25 goals for the season, while Miami extended its winning streak to three matches.

Oct. 14: Inter Miami 2-0 NYCFC
No goals, but after a scoreless first half, Messi helped break the deadlock by setting up Rodrigo De Paul for the opening goal. Germán Berterame later doubled Miami's advantage as the Herons secured their second consecutive win and clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs.

Oct. 10: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United

Back in the pink of Inter Miami, and back in the goals for Messi.

His two strikes sealed an emphatic 4-0 win for the Herons over D.C. United at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

After Luis Suárez had Miami 2-0 up after 39 minutes Messi scored his first in the 47th, retrieving a pass from the Uruguayan before tapping in a shot inside the right post.

Messi then padded the hosts' lead in the 60th minute, latching on to Rodrigo De Paul's pass, before dribbling inside the area, eluding two United defenders and firing past goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami
Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Valkyries even WNBA Finals as defense shuts down Dream
stories.summary: The Valkyries played stellar defense to beat the Dream and even the WNBA Finals at 2-2.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- Gabby Williams scored 17 points as the Golden State Valkyries played stellar defense to beat the Atlanta Dream 67-62 on Saturday and even the WNBA Finals at 2-2.

The best-of-seven series moves back to California on Monday for Game 5.

The Valkyries stymied Dream star Angel Reese, holding her to eight points. She had dominated the previous two games, averaging 25.5 points and 14.0 rebounds in the Dream victories. Reese struggled in Game 4, missing 10 of her 12 shots, including a few layups in the fourth quarter, after having double-doubles in each of the first three games.

Atlanta trimmed a 16-point halftime deficit to 61-55 midway through the fourth quarter, bringing fans in the sellout crowd of over 17,000 to their feet. Golden State answered with a 3-pointer by Veronica Burton to briefly silence them.

The Dream then scored seven of the next nine points, including a three-point play by Rhyne Howard with 28 seconds left to get within 66-62. Burton made the first of two free throws a second later, and Atlanta couldn't convert on the other end.

Howard finished with 19 points for Atlanta, which shot 33.3% overall and 4-for-23 from 3-point range.

Led defensively by Kiah Stokes, they challenged Atlanta shots and limited the Dream to few second-chance opportunities. Stokes finished with three blocks and now has a WNBA Finals record of 14 in the four games, surpassing the previous record of 12 by Brittney Griner and Sylvia Fowles.

Offensively, they limited turnovers, which had led to easy points for Atlanta in its two victories. The Valkyries also crashed the offensive boards, rebounding their own misses to give themselves more chances to score. Stokes had eight offensive rebounds of her 16 total.

Coach Natalie Nakase also made a change in the starting lineup, inserting Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles for Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini. While the Valkyries got off to a slow start again in the early-afternoon tipoff, Thornton and Zandalasini paid immediate dividends when they entered the game.

The two helped key a first-quarter run that gave Golden State its first lead since the third quarter of Game 2. Atlanta got within 24-20 on Reese's basket -- her lone one of the first half -- but the Valkyries responded with an 18-6 run to close the half.

The 42-26 deficit at the break was the largest gap the Dream had faced all playoffs.

Atlanta had dominated the third quarter in the WNBA Finals, outscoring Golden State 60-35 then in the first three games. The Valkyries wouldn't let them do that in Game 4, keeping a nine-point lead going into the fourth.

stories.headline: Connor Hellebuyck glad to join Devils after Jets standoff forced trade
stories.summary: Saying that "sitting at home for so long was getting to me," new Devils goaltender Connor Hellebuyck expressed his eagerness to play for New Jersey.
stories.body:
NEWARK, N.J. -- Connor Hellebuyck is joining the New Jersey Devils and is very happy about it.

The 33-year-old, three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender met the media before New Jersey faced the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday, and his eagerness to wear No. 37 for the Devils was evident.

"Sitting at home for so long was getting to me. For myself, I'm just really excited to play hockey again," Hellebuyck said after his suspension by the Winnipeg Jets for his failure to report to training camp led to Friday's trade to the Devils. "I'm joining a very skilled group. They brought me for a certain specific role. I'm really excited to fill that role, not only on the ice but off the ice as well."

Hellebuyck spent 11 seasons with the Jets, including a Presidents' Trophy-winning season in 2024-25, and helped the United States win gold at the Milan Cortina Olympics this year. A fifth-round draft pick in 2012 by Winnipeg, Hellebuyck is fifth on the U.S.-born goaltenders list with 345 career wins. Among U.S.-born goalies with 300 or more career starts, his .916 save percentage ranks fourth and 2.58 goals-against average ranks sixth.

Hellebuyck will share goaltending duties with 36-year-old Jake Allen.

The Devils sent forward Dawson Mercer, goalie Nico Daws, prospect Alexander Command, a 2029 second-round pick, a 2027 seventh-rounder and injured forward Nick Bjugstad to Winnipeg for Hellebuyck.

"Obviously having a goaltender of this pedigree come in here and support Jake is exciting," Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said. "That should give the group more confidence."

General manager Sunny Mehta said Hellebuyck's excitement for his new destination was palpable within minutes of their initial conversation.

Hellebuyck had been skating in Michigan while trade talks continued. He has five seasons left on a seven-year contract with an annual salary cap hit of $8.5 million.

"He was like: 'I'm ready, I'm packed. I'll get in my car right now,'" Mehta said about his exchange with his new goalie.

Mehta laughed and said he told Hellebuyck: "Don't do that."

Mehta has been trying to improve a team that missed the playoffs two of the past three seasons and has won one playoff series since 2012. New Jersey has won six of its first 10 games this season.

"Everything is about winning. That is my goal every single day," Mehta said. "This obviously makes us a better team. In my view it improves our team -- and I was thrilled about my team coming out of camp."

When Hellebuyck will play his first game for New Jersey is still undetermined. He hasn't played in an NHL game since April 13, a 6-2 Jets loss to the Vegas Golden Knights. Winnipeg missed the playoffs last spring a year after finishing with an NHL-best 116 points, when Hellebuyck won 47 games.

Hellebuyck said it's too early to address his feelings toward the city of Winnipeg and Jets fans. New Jersey visits Winnipeg on Nov. 10.

"There's a lot I need to say," he said. "Out of respect for them and the celebration of hockey, I'm going to postpone to a later date. I hope they know I care about them."

Hellebuyck said winning gold with his now-teammate Jack Hughes -- who scored the overtime goal against Canada for the Americans' first gold medal since the 1980 "Miracle on Ice" team -- has left an indelible mark on him.

"That's one of those moments and memories that I will cherish forever. And I will probably hear how other people will cherish them forever," Hellebuyck said. "One of my favorite stories is, 'Where were you when?' People will tell me what they were doing during the gold medal game. Those are my favorite stories to hear."

The veteran netminder, a native of Commerce, Michigan, who played two seasons of college hockey at UMass-Lowell, said he looks forward to playing home games in the U.S. after more than a decade calling Canada home.

"I know I'm going to get a lot more of that here than in Canada because I don't think they care much about it," Hellebuyck said of the gold medal plaudits for the Olympic win over Canada. "This is closer to my family's home. Just being in the USA will be very exciting for this next chapter in my career."

stories.headline: United States Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Austin, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.
stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Texas for the United States Grand Prix, with the championship battle set to heat up at the Circuit of the Americas.

Max Verstappen claimed his second victory this season after winning the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli continued to extend his lead in the title championship to 102 points from Mercedes teammate George Russell, and there is a mathematical chance he will be able to clinch the title in Austin.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 18th round.

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How F1's next rookie could shake up Ferrari's future

- F1 still planning Middle East finale amid Kimi Antonelli title uncertainty - sources

- Franco Colapinto urges fans to stop 'attacking' Formula 1 drivers on social media

United States Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 23

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc sets pace in second practice from Kimi Antonelli

Saturday, October 24

Final Practice: 6.30 p.m. - 7.30 p.m.

Qualifying: 10 p.m. - 11 p.m.

Sunday, October 25

United States Grand Prix: 8 p.m. (GMT)

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the United States Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

It's a mix of fast corners, long straights and has one of the steepest elevation climbs to Turn 1.

United States Grand Prix

Circuit: Circuit of the Americas; Austin, Texas

Previous winners in United States

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2016: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2017: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2018: Kimi Räikkönen (Ferrari)

2019: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)

2021: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2023: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2024: Charles Leclerc (Ferrari)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2012

Lap record: 1:36.169, Charles Leclerc (2019)

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Most wins: Lewis Hamilton with six (2007, 2012, 2014-2017) Other winners from the current grid are Verstappen (2021-2023, 2025) and Leclerc (2024).

Most poles: Hamilton (2007, 2016-2018) is tied with Michael Schumacher (2000-2002, 2006) on four. Other pole sitters from the current grid are Verstappen (2021 and 2025), Carlos Sainz (2022), Leclerc (2023) and Lando Norris (2024).

Weather forecast

The weather for the United States Grand Prix is expected to be light rain with a gentle breeze throughout the course of the weekend, with highs of 32°C.

What happened last time out?
Verstappen edged out Norris to take an imperious pole position by 0.291 seconds.

The Red Bull driver dominated the race and posed as a serious threat to McLaren's Norris and Oscar Piastri in the drivers' championship.

Norris finished second and cut his lead to 14 points to Piastri in the standings, who finished fifth. Verstappen ended the weekend only 40 points behind Piastri with five races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.

stories.headline: Magic's Paolo Banchero has ankle sprain; out multiple weeks, sources say
stories.summary: Magic star Paolo Banchero has sustained a low-grade high ankle sprain, the team announced, with sources telling ESPN that the forward will miss multiple weeks.
stories.body:
Orlando Magic star Paolo Banchero has sustained a low-grade high ankle sprain, the team announced Saturday, with sources telling ESPN's Shams Charania that the forward will miss multiple weeks.

This injury diagnosis typically carries a timetable of four to six weeks.

Banchero was injured in the first half of Friday night's 115-93 loss to the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves. He told The Orlando Sentinel after the game that he began experiencing discomfort in the first quarter.

He sat out the fourth quarter and finished with 14 points and six rebounds.

Last season, the Magic outscored opponents by 45 points in the 182 minutes that Banchero, Franz Wagner, Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane and Wendell Carter Jr. were on the court together. They collectively shot 50.1% from the field and 36.4% from 3-point range while holding opponents to 46.2% overall shooting and 34.5% 3-point shooting.

The Magic are 40-26 over the past three regular seasons when the quartet of Banchero, Wagner, Suggs and Carter all play. They went 7-3 in 10 games without Banchero last season.

Over the past two seasons combined, Banchero has missed 46 games, Wagner 70 and Suggs 72, yet the Magic still reached the playoffs both years.

Banchero was off to a flying start this season, averaging team highs of 24.5 points and 7.5 assists per game, along with 6.5 rebounds and doing all that on 70% shooting.

For his career, the 2022 No. 1 draft pick and 2024 All-Star is averaging 22.4 points, 7.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game for Orlando.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
Penrith have informed Luron Patea's management of their desire to retain the young prop beyond 2027, although he still intends to test the open market from November 1.

ESPN understands multiple clubs are interested in speaking to Patea, who is approaching the final year of his Panthers contract.

ESPN previously reported that Penrith had yet to begin extension discussions with Patea.

Tigers keen to retain Mason

Wests Tigers are keen to retain Heath Mason, with the club working through roster space to accommodate the young utility.

ESPN understands Mason remains part of the Tigers' long-term plans, although his future is yet to be resolved ahead of 2027.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.
